newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Wounded Israeli schoolgirl recalls Jordanian gunman.
newsitem.headline: Wounded Israeli schoolgirl recalls Jordanian gunman.

text.p: Fourteen-year-old Hila Ivri laid next to her twin sister in hospital on Thursday and relived how a "bad guy with big eyes" shot them on a field trip to a Jordan border site nicknamed "The Island of Peace".
Seven Israeli teenagers were killed and at least six wounded by a Jordanian soldier who sprayed automatic weapons fire at a school group.

"All the girls screamed and cried and ran beneath bushes to hide. Many girls were hurt and bloody. I was hit in the leg," said Ivri at a hospital in northern Israel. Her sister was shot in the stomach.
"I saw the gunman. He held his gun. He was shooting, and then he started shooting again...He was a bad guy with big eyes," she said.
"I saw one girl who was hit in the shoulder. She rolled over the bushes and then stopped breathing."
Jordanian authorities were briefing Israeli teachers in the group when a uniformed Jordanian standing on a hill above them took aim and emptied an entire ammunition clip.
"It was like war, girls hit in the throat, in the neck, in the stomach, on their legs," said teacher Zacharya Ozeri, clutching a denim school bag he said belonged to one of the dead girls.

Some of the girls called home immediately on mobile phones and alerted the school in Beit Shemesh, a working class town near Jerusalem, where parents gathered to find out if their children were wounded.
"I simply can't bury these small children. It's devastating," said teacher Pnina Cohen outside the school. Some of the girls were to be buried later on Thursday.
Students at the school burst into tears when word spread of the shooting.
Later, dazed survivors -- some of them scratched after taking cover during the shooting -- hugged their parents in an emotional reunion outside the school.

"We were told school groups travelled in the area daily...it was a quiet area," said principal Moshe Ablovich. But Israel's Education Ministry said it never approved field trips to the site because of security concerns.
"Tomorrow will be a regular school day...and each class will meet with its teacher and a psychologist so the children can release their emotions," Ablovich told reporters.
Witness Rosa Himi said the carnage could have been heavier.

"We yelled for the girls to get down and we all tried to hide," Himi said. "(The gunman) came down and started chasing us. I saw how he inserted a new clip but with the second one he didn't manage to fire."
Ozeri said the students called for help but Jordanian authorities blocked Israelis from entering the area.
"I yelled at them in Arabic to stop him, to do something... They didn't do a thing."
Under a 1994 peace treaty with Jordan, Israel leases the farmland where the attack took place. Entry is through a Jordanian checkpoint.
